Each row has two squares that are adjacent to each other, so a row holds at most one marked square. With 10 rows and 9 marked squares, exactly one row is empty and every other row has exactly one mark, in the left (L) or right (R) column.

Two marked squares in vertically adjacent rows must be in different columns. So within each run of consecutive non-empty rows, the marks must alternate L/R. A run of length at least 1 therefore has 2 choices, and an empty run has 1.

The empty row at position k splits the rows into runs of lengths k−1 and 10−k. These runs are not adjacent to each other, so their choices are independent.

- k = 1: the runs have lengths 0 and 9, giving 1·2 = 2 ways.
- k = 10: likewise 2 ways.
- k = 2 through 9 (8 values): both runs are non-empty, giving 2·2 = 4 ways each, so 32 ways.

Total: 2 + 2 + 32 = 36.

ANSWER: 36
